Sternoclavicular injury: 2

A patient has medial clavicular pain after a collision, accompanied by dysphagia and shortness of breath. The team is concerned about compression of structures behind the sternum. Which displacement direction is the dangerous possibility?

  1. Posterior medial-clavicle displacement
  2. Anterior medial-clavicle displacement
  3. Medial clavicular physeal injury
  4. CT assessment of the SC region
  5. Urgent reduction with appropriate specialist support
Answer and explanation

Posterior medial-clavicle displacement

Posterior displacement can compress the trachea, esophagus and major vessels.

Option explanations

Posterior medial-clavicle displacement: Posterior displacement can compress the trachea, esophagus and major vessels.

Anterior medial-clavicle displacement: Anterior SC dislocation commonly produces a palpable prominence over the joint. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Medial clavicular physeal injury: The late-closing medial clavicular physis can mimic SC dislocation in young patients. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

CT assessment of the SC region: Plain radiographs can be difficult to interpret; CT defines SC displacement and adjacent anatomy. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Urgent reduction with appropriate specialist support: Posterior SC dislocation requires a controlled setting because manipulation can endanger adjacent major vessels. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
